brief_rule: Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy; each brief names the trait kept and the trait changed. GPL donor: shape and idea only; no code copied.
inspiration: Server-timed animation: the client stretches the attack clip so its length matches the server's attack time, so the server owns the timing and the client only plays it. For rows 6 and 7. File: src/Engine/MapEngine/Entity.js lines 629-642.

Lead-time projectile: a bow shot starts its effect after a lead computed from the motion, so the arrow leaves with the swing. Keep the lead as its own value (the donor edits the received packet in place at line 647; defect for us). For rows 10 and 13. File: Entity.js lines 645-656.
Weapon trail per weapon class: one trail look chosen by weapon class from a table, with our own palette. For row 15 (gear dressing) and row 10. File: src/DB/Items/WeaponTrailTable.js lines 16-26.
Shadow scale per creature from a small id-keyed table, sized to the creature's footprint, with flying creatures at zero. For readability at 375 wide. File: src/DB/Monsters/ShadowTable.js lines 12-14.

Projectile look chosen by creature job from a lookup table, so a ranged creature gets its own shot without a new code path. For rows 7 and 13. Files: src/DB/Monsters/AttackEffectTable.js line 10; Entity.js line 657.

Replay as tagged fields: the parser reads known field ids and skips unknown ones, so old replays still load. For row 19 (fight record and replay). File: src/Engine/Replay/ReplayParser.js lines 487-506.

briefs.label: Server-stretched swing
briefs.why: A hero's swing that always lasts exactly the time the server allows makes the hit land when the swing ends, which reads clearly at 375 wide because the body's motion and the hit moment line up.
briefs.keep: The server sets the swing time; the client stretches or squeezes the clip to match it.
briefs.change: Our hit is decided by the engine tick and the client only plays the clip; the clip has a fixed hit frame that is not scaled; a fight camera cue fires on the hit frame.

briefs.label: Arrow with a lead
briefs.why: An arrow that leaves a fraction after the bow draw looks like it was loosed by the body, not spawned at the target, and it stays readable against a crowd.
briefs.keep: A projectile starts after a lead computed from the motion; the lead is a field of the shot.
briefs.change: Our lead is a per-weapon catalogue value, not a change to the server packet; the arrow is a short bright streak, not the donor's effect.

briefs.label: Trail per blade class
briefs.why: A swing trail whose look depends on the blade class lets a player read the weapon at a glance during a fast fight, without extra UI.
briefs.keep: One trail look per weapon class, chosen by a table entry.
briefs.change: Our trails use our own palette (cool for blades, warm for blunt weapons); trail length follows swing speed; no donor trail names.

briefs.label: Footprint shadow table
briefs.why: A shadow sized from the creature's footprint, with flying creatures at no shadow, keeps the ground readable at a glance on a phone.
briefs.keep: A small id-keyed scale table for shadows.
briefs.change: We size from our silhouette width at 375 wide, and flying creatures use a ring below them instead of a shadow.

briefs.label: Fight record with tagged fields
briefs.why: A fight record made of id-tagged fields lets the replay format grow without breaking old recordings, which matters for a long-lived fight log.
briefs.keep: Known fields by id; unknown fields skipped.
briefs.change: Our fields are attack time, hit, guard, parry and server tick, not the donor's ids; the record has its own version byte.

defects_found.defect: The received attack time is changed in place (pkt.attackMT += delayTime) and later read as the start tick, so the packet no longer holds the server value.
defects_found.fix: keep the server attack time and the lead as separate fields.
